source.paraphrase: A binding used only as a type should be imported as a type, so the emit does not keep a value import the program never calls.

invariants.why: Fidelity: same-file proxy. A value import whose uses in this file are only type positions is reported. The compiler half is verbatimModuleSyntax on TS-CFG-001. This check warns because it cannot see another file.
invariants.fixHint: Write import type, or import { type Name }. Turn on verbatimModuleSyntax in tsconfig so the compiler checks the same choice across files.
invariants.avoid: An unused import is not reported. A namespace import is not classified. typeof Name is a value use. A use in another file is invisible. import type and an inline type specifier already match this rule.

source.paraphrase: If a binding is never assigned again, const says so. let promises a later assignment that does not exist.

invariants.why: Fidelity: same-file. A let with no assignment, update, or destructuring assignment in this file should be const. Mutation such as push is not a reassignment, so the binding is still const. var and parameter mutation belong to senior, not this rule.
invariants.fixHint: Change the let to const. If the binding is assigned later in this file, keep let.
invariants.avoid: A for-loop i++ is a reassignment. An inner let is a different binding from an outer one with the same name. An assignment in another file, including to an export, is invisible. declare let is skipped. push, index writes, and property writes do not count as reassignment.

source.locator: do not prefix interfaces with I
source.paraphrase: An I prefix names the declaration kind. The interface should be named for the concept.

invariants.why: Fidelity: spelling. An interface whose name matches I followed by a capital letter is reported, exported or not. This warns because ID and similar abbreviations are the same spelling and the rule cannot tell them apart.
invariants.fixHint: Drop the I. User stays User. Keep names such as Input, Image, and I18n; they do not match.
invariants.avoid: I18n does not match because the character after I is a digit. Input, Image, and Id do not match. The rule does not look at type aliases or classes.

source.paraphrase: A value that crossed a text boundary is unknown until a parser returns a typed value. A cast only claims the type.

invariants.why: Fidelity: state, same function. JSON.parse and any call named json start tainted. A later parse, safeParse, validate, decode, parseAsync, or safeParseAsync clears the binding. as T, other than as unknown alone, and a type annotation other than unknown are typed uses. An if keeps the taint when either branch leaves it tainted. This warns because a method named json is not always Response.json.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the value through a parser before the annotation or the cast. as unknown is not a parser. schema.parse and schema.safeParse clear the binding.
invariants.avoid: The check follows bindings and aliases in source order in this file only. A method named json that does not read a response is still tainted, so a typed use of it is a false positive. An untyped return is not a finding. as unknown as User is a finding on the outer cast. A parser named something else is not recognized.

source.paraphrase: A function that takes an array it only reads should say so. A mutable array type allows sort, reverse, and push on the caller's value.

invariants.why: The outermost array of a directly exported function or arrow parameter, and of a property on a directly exported interface or type alias, must be readonly T[] or ReadonlyArray<T>. The same applies to an array property inside the type of such a parameter. TS-READONLY-001 is a different, opt-in rule about every public property.
invariants.fixHint: Write readonly string[] or ReadonlyArray<string>. Copy before sorting. A readonly modifier on the property does not make the array readonly.
invariants.avoid: Nested arrays inside an outer ReadonlyArray are not walked. Class methods are not included. A function that is only re-exported by export { load } is not seen. A local function is not included.

source.paraphrase: sort and reverse mutate the array they are called on. A parameter is the caller's array unless the function copies it first.

invariants.why: A direct sort or reverse on an identifier that resolves to a parameter mutates the caller. [...items].sort(), items.slice().sort(), and toSorted or toReversed do not. The receiver has to be that identifier, parentheses included.
invariants.fixHint: Copy first: return [...items].sort() or return items.toSorted(). toReversed is the copy for reverse.
invariants.avoid: const alias = items; alias.sort() is not seen, because the receiver is not the parameter identifier. items[0] and a method call other than sort or reverse are not this rule. A local array is not a parameter.

source.paraphrase: A thrown error can carry the error that caused it. A rethrow that drops the caught value drops the stack.

invariants.why: Every throw inside a catch must pass an object property named cause, either as a pair or as a shorthand. Empty catch stays clean-code CC-ER-002. A throw that is not inside catch is not this rule, and TS-THROW-001 still owns throws on an exported boundary.
invariants.fixHint: throw new Error("failed", { cause: error }) or throw new Error("failed", { cause }).
invariants.avoid: The cause property has to be a direct argument object of the thrown call, or the thrown object itself. A cause nested inside another call is not accepted. Putting the caught value in the message does not count.

source.locator: suppress a line with a reason
source.paraphrase: @ts-expect-error and @ts-ignore hide a compiler diagnostic. The comment has to say why the line is exempt.

invariants.why: A comment that is only @ts-expect-error or @ts-ignore has no reason. TS-IGNORE-001 still forbids @ts-ignore outright. core EVA-SUP-001 ratchets new suppressions. This rule is the missing reason, including on @ts-expect-error, which the ignore ban allows.
invariants.fixHint: Write the reason on the same comment: // @ts-expect-error the generated type is wrong.
invariants.avoid: @ts-nocheck is not this rule. A reason is any non-space text after the directive. A reasoned @ts-ignore still fails TS-IGNORE-001 when that rule is on. The reason is not checked for truth.

source.paraphrase: any disables the checker for everything it touches. A file should not gain more of them.

invariants.why: Diff ratchet, no-increase. The count is syntax nodes of the any type. Existing any stays. A new any, including Array<any>, denies. TS-ANY-001 remains the opt-in ban and stays off. Comments and strings do not count. This count is separate from the non-null count so the two cannot cancel.
invariants.fixHint: Name the type, or use unknown and narrow it. Do not add any to pay for removing a non-null assertion.
invariants.avoid: The finding is the file's new total, reported on line 1. A comment that says any, or the string "any", is not a type. pregate-allow-any does not lower this count.

source.paraphrase: A postfix ! tells the checker a value is present. The file should not gain more of those claims.

invariants.why: Diff ratchet, no-increase. The count is non-null syntax nodes. Existing assertions stay. A new one denies. TS-BANG-001 remains the opt-in ban and stays off. value!! counts twice. This count is separate from the any count.
invariants.fixHint: Narrow with a conditional, or change the type so the value is present. Do not add ! to pay for removing an any.
invariants.avoid: The finding is the file's new total, reported on line 1. !== is a comparison, not this operator. A comment that contains ! is not an assertion.
